# The apt packages the Dispatch browser suite installs for Playwright: Playwright's whole
# ubuntu24.04-x64 list, which is the union of the `tools`, `chromium`, `firefox` and `webkit`
# entries of that table in playwright-core's lib/coreBundle.js. Nothing is left out of it.
#
# This file held that list less four media packages until dispatch://INFRA-1506
# (cybermonklabs/legion#2888) put the whole list back: WebKit plays video and audio through
# GStreamer, so without gstreamer1.0-plugins-good, gstreamer1.0-plugins-bad, gstreamer1.0-libav
# and libavcodec60 it loads a page and plays nothing. What each of those four carries, and the
# decoder guard that proves they reached the GStreamer registry, are in the head of
# .github/scripts/playwright-install.sh, the script that reads this file.
#
# Measured in job 128209099649, of cybermonklabs/legion#2888 at 5ff42456: the 79 names below and
# gstreamer1.0-tools resolve, with their dependencies, to 182 packages and 114 MB of archives
# (`0 upgraded, 182 newly installed, 0 to remove and 27 not upgraded.` and `Need to get 114 MB
# of archives.`).
#
# gstreamer1.0-tools is not one of these names. It is the one package the install adds that
# Playwright's list does not name - it carries the `gst-inspect-1.0` the decoder guard runs -
# and it is held apart, in the script's `step_tools`, because this file is what
# .github/scripts/playwright-deps-current.sh holds against Playwright's own list, name for name.
#
# One script reads it, .github/scripts/playwright-install.sh, which the "Install the lane's
# Playwright browsers" step of .github/workflows/dispatch-browser.yaml's shard job and of its
# alone job both run; its `grep` drops these `#` lines and the blank ones. That filter is
# load-bearing: the shell reads this file, not apt, and `$packages` is left unquoted there and
# splits into words, so a comment line reaches apt as one package name per word. That script
# then holds this list against Playwright's own with .github/scripts/playwright-deps-current.sh.
#
# On a Playwright upgrade, re-derive the list as that union again, with nothing taken out of it.
# Deriving it at run time by subtracting one apt closure from another does not work and must not
# be written: the closure of the four that carry playback and the closure of the rest share 35
# packages Playwright's own list names or needs, and the subtraction leaves WebKit unable to
# launch. That paragraph is a standing refusal, not a record of a design that was taken out:
# nobody is to re-derive a reduced list.
